# Task: a tag on each note

Notes get a tag, such as `home` or `work`. `store.mojo` already keeps it
(`Note.tag`, and `Store.add(owner, text, tag)`), and the journal has a column
for it; the web layer does not build against it yet.

Make the API take a tag when a note is created, required:
`POST /notes` with `{"text":"buy milk","tag":"home"}`. Every note the API
answers carries its tag after its text:
`{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk","tag":"home"}`. A body without a
tag is a `400`. Update `API.md` to match.
# Notes API

The contract the notes service keeps with its clients. Every answer below is
relied on by a client; a change to one is a change to this document first.

## Every route

- A request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the scheme is matched
  in any case (`bearer` too). The service reads its tokens at start-up, one
  `token user` pair per line of its tokens file.
- A missing, malformed or unknown token: `401`, body `Unauthorized`, and the
  field `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- A note is visible to its owner only: anyone else gets the same `404` as for
  a note that does not exist.
- JSON is sent and received as `Content-Type: application/json`. A note is
  `{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk"}`, its members in that order.
- A request the service cannot read (a path value that is not a number, a
  JSON body that is malformed or lacks a member) is `400`, body
  `Bad Request`, with its cause written to the service's standard error.

## Routes

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /notes` | `200`, the caller's notes, oldest first: `[{"id":1,...}]`, or `[]` |
| `GET /notes/{id}` | `200`, the note; `404`, body `no note {id}`, when there is none the caller owns |
| `POST /notes`, body `{"text":"..."}` | `201`, the note as stored, with its new id; `422`, body `text too long`, when the text is longer than the service's limit in bytes |

## Storage

Notes are kept in a journal file and read back at start-up. A note whose write
fails is not kept: the client gets `503`, body `storage unavailable`, the
cause is written to standard error, and the next write succeeds once the
journal can be written again. The next note takes the id the failed one did
not use.

## Running the service

    PROGRAM PORT JOURNAL TOKENS MAX_TEXT

`MAX_TEXT` is the longest text accepted, in bytes.
#!/bin/sh
# Builds ./notes from notes_flare.mojo.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec /root/.pixi/bin/pixi run --manifest-path /home/user/muntin/pixi.toml --frozen -e flare mojo build -I . notes_flare.mojo -o notes
#!/bin/sh
# Serves ./notes on 127.0.0.1:PORT (default 8080), its journal in
# journal.log, its tokens in tokens (t-ada is ada, t-bo is bo), texts
# up to 40 bytes.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec ./notes "${1:-8080}" journal.log tokens 40

README.md-40-## Why flare
README.md-41-
README.md-42-- **Batteries included:** HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 over QUIC (server + client), WebSocket (RFC 6455 + permessage-deflate), gRPC, TLS 1.2/1.3 + mTLS + in-process HTTPS termination (`bind_tls` + `serve`), streaming responses on every wire (one handler streams byte-identically over h1 / h2 / h3 / https), sessions, gzip + brotli, CORS, static files, SSE, templates, RFC 9111 caching, and an OpenAPI 3.1 emitter. Full inventory in [`docs/features.md`](docs/features.md).
README.md:43:- **Composable by types, not callbacks:** `Handler` is a trait; `Router`, middleware, and typed extractors (`PathInt`, `JsonAs[T]`, `Cookies`, ...) compose by nesting structs, monomorphised into one direct call sequence per request type with no virtual dispatch.
README.md-44-- **Hard to misuse under load:** Per-request `Cancel` tokens, graceful drain, sanitized 4xx/5xx, TLS cert reload, structured logging, Prometheus metrics, and an in-process `TestClient[H]`.
README.md-45-- **Fast, with a tight tail:** Thread-per-core reactor (`kqueue` / `epoll`, opt-in `io_uring`); top-of-pack throughput with a p99 median that ties `actix_web` and beats `hyper` / `axum`, plus [match-or-beat-quiche on HTTP/3](#performance).
README.md-46-- **Fuzzed:** 63 fuzz harnesses, 9M+ runs, zero known crashes; ASan + assert-mode coverage on every FFI boundary.

input.message:
Notes now take a required tag, and every note the API returns includes it. `./build.sh` succeeds, and I tested the change against a running server.

**What was wrong:** `store.mojo` had already changed to `Store.add(owner, text, tag)`, but the web layer still called `add(owner, text)`. So `notes_flare.mojo` didn't compile, and the request body had no tag field.

**What I changed:**
- The request body struct (`NewNote`) now has a `tag` field after `text`, and the create handler passes it to `store.add`.
- Notes are sent back by the JSON codec straight from `store.mojo`'s `Note`, which already has `tag` after `text`. So the GET and POST answers needed no further code.
- A missing `text` or `tag` was already rejected by the framework with `400`, body `Bad Request`, and the cause on standard error. That matches the existing rule in `API.md`.

**Test results (ports 20080 and 20081):**
- `POST {"text":"buy milk","tag":"home"}` returns `201` with `{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk","tag":"home"}`. The single-note `GET`, the list `GET` and the journal all show the tag.
- These bodies return `400`: no tag, no text, a tag of `5`, and a tag of `null`.
- Members sent in a different order are accepted. Tabs, quotes and newlines in a tag survive the journal.
- Tags are read back after a restart.
- The other rules still hold: `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, the lower-case `bearer` scheme, `404` for another user's note, `400` for `/notes/abc`, `422` for text that is too long, and `503` when the journal can't be written, with the next write succeeding afterwards.

All the servers I started have been stopped. I deleted the `journal.log` my tests created, since there wasn't one before.

**Files changed:**
- `/srv/runs/r08/notes_flare.mojo`
- `/srv/runs/r08/API.md`: the note shape now includes `"tag"`, and `POST /notes` takes `{"text":"...","tag":"..."}` with both members required, answering `400` when either is missing or not a string.

**Things I'm unsure of:**
- **Empty tag:** `"tag":""` is accepted. I read "required" as "the member must be present". If an empty tag should be rejected, that needs one more check.
- **Tag length:** tags have no length limit. The 40-byte limit applies only to the text.
- **Old journals:** a journal written before this change has three columns per line. `Store.open` reads a fourth column, so it would likely crash at start-up. That code is the other team's, so I didn't touch it.
- **Server shutdown:** when I tested two servers on one port at once, the second bound alongside the first instead of failing. The first also ignored my first SIGTERM and stopped on the second. If you run tests the same way, check that the server you are talking to is the one you just started.
